children: Passenger vehicle demand remains strong, while inflation and rising input costs could weigh on the sector’s outlook

India’s automobile industry is likely to see near-term support from inventory build-up ahead of the festive season, but sales growth could moderate thereafter as the sector faces a high base, according to a report by JM Financial Institutional Securities.
The report said demand remains healthy across major vehicle segments, although growth has been stronger in passenger vehicles than in two-wheelers.
Domestic passenger vehicle (PV) volumes increased 37 per cent year-on-year in August 2026, while volumes during the first five months of FY27 rose 30 per cent.

Utility vehicles (UVs) continued to account for a large part of this growth. UV volumes increased 46 per cent year-on-year in August, taking their share of overall passenger vehicle sales to about 69 per cent from around 65 per cent a year earlier.
JM Financial said continued demand for UVs is likely to remain an important driver for passenger vehicle growth, with automakers having a wider SUV portfolio positioned to benefit from the trend.

Two-wheeler demand remained resilient but showed a slower pace of growth in August. Domestic internal combustion engine (ICE) two-wheeler sales grew 5 per cent year-on-year during the month, while FY27 year-to-date growth stood at 14 per cent.

Within motorcycles, premium segments continued to see stronger demand. Sales in the 150–250cc segment increased 28 per cent during FY27 so far, while motorcycles above 250cc grew 34 per cent. The sub-125cc segment recorded growth of about 6 per cent.
The brokerage attributed part of the August moderation to the later start of the festive season this year.
West Asia Conflict Adds Cost Risk

The report also highlighted inflation and input costs as risks for the industry. JM Financial said sustained inflationary pressures amid the ongoing West Asia conflict remain a key variable to monitor.
While festive inventory build-up could support wholesale volumes in the near term, the brokerage expects growth rates to normalise against the higher base of the previous period.
